name: Thoracic duct
supplies_or_drains: lower limbs, abdomen, left thorax, left upper limb, left head and neck
notes: Drains roughly three-quarters of the body. Ascends from the cisterna chyli through the aortic hiatus, crosses to the left at about T5, and empties at the junction of the left subclavian and internal jugular veins. Injury during left neck dissection or oesophagectomy produces a chylous leak.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Right lymphatic duct
supplies_or_drains: right upper limb, right head and neck, right thorax
notes: Drains the remaining quarter of the body into the junction of the right subclavian and internal jugular veins. About a centimetre long, and often absent as a single vessel -- its three trunks may open separately.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Cisterna chyli
supplies_or_drains: lumbar and intestinal lymphatic trunks
notes: A saccular dilatation at about L1-L2, behind and to the right of the aorta. Receives the intestinal trunk carrying chyle, which is why chylous effusions look milky after a fatty meal.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Lumbar lymphatic trunks
supplies_or_drains: lower limbs, pelvis, kidneys, adrenal glands, abdominal wall
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Intestinal lymphatic trunk
supplies_or_drains: stomach, intestine, pancreas, spleen, part of the liver
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Jugular lymphatic trunk, left
supplies_or_drains: left head and neck, from the deep cervical nodes
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Subclavian lymphatic trunk, left
supplies_or_drains: left upper limb, from the apical axillary nodes
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Bronchomediastinal lymphatic trunk, left
supplies_or_drains: left lung, heart, thymus, oesophagus and thoracic wall
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Jugular lymphatic trunk, right
supplies_or_drains: right head and neck, from the deep cervical nodes
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Subclavian lymphatic trunk, right
supplies_or_drains: right upper limb, from the apical axillary nodes
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Deep cervical lymph nodes (levels I-VI)
supplies_or_drains: head and neck, via the superficial node groups
notes: Arranged along the internal jugular vein. The jugulodigastric (tonsillar) and jugulo-omohyoid (tongue) nodes are the named sentinel members. Level classification drives neck dissection planning in head and neck cancer.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Axillary lymph nodes (levels I-III)
supplies_or_drains: upper limb
breast
anterolateral trunk wall
notes: Levels are defined by pectoralis minor: level I lateral to it, level II behind it, level III medial. This is the staging basis in breast cancer, and the reason axillary clearance carries a lymphoedema risk that sentinel node biopsy avoids.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Cubital (supratrochlear) lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: ulnar side of the forearm and hand, along the basilic vein
notes: Palpable above the medial epicondyle. Classically enlarged in secondary syphilis and in cat-scratch disease.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Deep inguinal lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: glans penis or clitoris
deep lower limb lymphatics
superficial inguinal nodes
notes: Lie medial to the femoral vein; the highest of them, sitting in the femoral canal, is the node of Cloquet.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Superficial inguinal lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: lower limb
lower abdominal wall
perineum
gluteal region
anal canal below the pectinate line
notes: Lie in the superficial fascia parallel to and below the inguinal ligament. Their perineal territory is why they enlarge in genital infection, and why anal carcinoma above versus below the pectinate line spreads to entirely different node groups.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Popliteal lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: lateral foot and posterolateral leg, along the small saphenous vein
notes: The lateral foot drains here first, whereas the medial foot drains directly to the superficial inguinal nodes along the great saphenous vein -- so the site of a foot lesion predicts which node group enlarges.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Bronchomediastinal lymphatic trunk, left
supplies_or_drains: left lung, heart, thymus, oesophagus and thoracic wall
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

gluteal region
anal canal below the pectinate line

name: Submental lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: chin, lower lip, floor of mouth, tip of tongue
notes: Floor of the submental triangle, between the anterior bellies of digastric. First echelon for anterior floor-of-mouth and tip-of-tongue cancer.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Submandibular lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: face, nose, upper and lateral lip, anterior tongue, submandibular and sublingual glands
notes: Lie against the submandibular gland in its fascial bed. First echelon for oral cavity and anterior tongue cancer; frequently removed with the gland in neck dissection.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Parotid lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: scalp (anterior and temporal), eyelids, external ear, parotid gland
notes: Preauricular and intraparotid nodes, the latter embedded within the gland itself and at risk in parotid surgery. First echelon for skin cancer of the temple, anterior scalp and ear.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Mastoid (retroauricular) lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: posterior scalp, posterior surface of the pinna, external auditory meatus
notes: Overlie the mastoid process. Enlarge in otitis externa and rubella; a classic finding on the posterior auricular exam.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Occipital lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: posterior scalp, skin over the occiput and upper neck
notes: Small group at the apex of the posterior triangle, along the occipital vessels.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Superficial cervical lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: skin over the parotid and mandibular region, lower ear, along the external jugular vein
notes: Run with the external jugular vein across sternocleidomastoid before draining into the deep cervical chain.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Submental lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: chin, lower lip, floor of mouth, tip of tongue
notes: Floor of the submental triangle, between the anterior bellies of digastric. First echelon for anterior floor-of-mouth and tip-of-tongue cancer.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Submandibular lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: face, nose, upper and lateral lip, anterior tongue, submandibular and sublingual glands
notes: Lie against the submandibular gland in its fascial bed. First echelon for oral cavity and anterior tongue cancer; frequently removed with the gland in neck dissection.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Parotid lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: scalp (anterior and temporal), eyelids, external ear, parotid gland
notes: Preauricular and intraparotid nodes, the latter embedded within the gland itself and at risk in parotid surgery. First echelon for skin cancer of the temple, anterior scalp and ear.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Mastoid (retroauricular) lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: posterior scalp, posterior surface of the pinna, external auditory meatus
notes: Overlie the mastoid process. Enlarge in otitis externa and rubella; a classic finding on the posterior auricular exam.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Occipital lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: posterior scalp, skin over the occiput and upper neck
notes: Small group at the apex of the posterior triangle, along the occipital vessels.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Superficial cervical lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: skin over the parotid and mandibular region, lower ear, along the external jugular vein
notes: Run with the external jugular vein across sternocleidomastoid before draining into the deep cervical chain.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Supraclavicular lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: lower neck, upper thorax, and (on the right) upper abdominal viscera via deep thoracic and abdominal collaterals
notes: Right-sided enlargement is less specific than left, but still raises the same visceral-malignancy concern.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Supraclavicular lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: lower neck, upper thorax, and abdominal and pelvic viscera via the thoracic duct terminus
notes: The left node (Virchow's/Troisier's node) sits where the thoracic duct empties into the venous angle, so it is a sentinel for gastric, pancreatic and other intra-abdominal malignancy -- a hard left supraclavicular node is a classic finding, not a curiosity.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Tracheobronchial lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: lungs, bronchi, and trachea
notes: Carinal and hilar groups; the first echelon for bronchogenic carcinoma and the nodes sampled at mediastinoscopy.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Paratracheal lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: trachea, esophagus, and thyroid gland
notes: Run alongside the trachea in the tracheoesophageal groove; the recurrent laryngeal nerve runs through this chain, so nodal disease here threatens the nerve directly.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Parasternal (internal thoracic) lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: medial breast, anterior chest wall, pleura, and diaphragm
notes: Along the internal thoracic vessels behind the costal cartilages. Second echelon for medial-quadrant breast cancer, parallel to the axillary route -- missed if only the axilla is staged.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Tracheobronchial lymph nodes

supplies_or_drains: trachea, esophagus, and thyroid gland

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Parasternal (internal thoracic) lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: medial breast, anterior chest wall, pleura, and diaphragm
notes: Along the internal thoracic vessels behind the costal cartilages. Second echelon for medial-quadrant breast cancer, parallel to the axillary route -- missed if only the axilla is staged.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Celiac lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: stomach, duodenum, pancreas, spleen, and liver, via the left gastric, hepatic and splenic node chains
notes: Cluster around the celiac trunk's origin from the aorta; the confluence point for the three named gastric/hepatic/splenic chains.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Superior mesenteric lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: jejunum, ileum, cecum, appendix, ascending and transverse colon
notes: Run in the mesentery alongside the superior mesenteric vessels; the longest node chain in the abdomen given the length of gut it serves.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Inferior mesenteric lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: descending colon, sigmoid colon, and upper rectum
notes: Along the inferior mesenteric vessels; staging nodes for left-sided colorectal cancer.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Lumbar (para-aortic) lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: kidney, adrenal gland, and gonad on that side, posterior abdominal wall, and the efferents of the common iliac chain
notes: Run alongside the aorta and IVC. The testis and ovary drain here directly, bypassing the pelvic nodes entirely, because both organs migrate from this level in development -- the reason testicular cancer is staged by the para-aortic chain, not the groin.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Lumbar (para-aortic) lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: kidney, adrenal gland, and gonad on that side, posterior abdominal wall, and the efferents of the common iliac chain
notes: Run alongside the aorta and IVC. The testis and ovary drain here directly, bypassing the pelvic nodes entirely, because both organs migrate from this level in development -- the reason testicular cancer is staged by the para-aortic chain, not the groin.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Common iliac lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: the external and internal iliac node groups on that side
notes: Receive both the external and internal iliac chains before draining to the para-aortic nodes; a common site of nodal disease in cervical, prostate and bladder cancer staging.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: External iliac lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: deep inguinal nodes, bladder, proximal urethra, prostate or cervix, and lower anterior abdominal wall
notes: Lie along the external iliac vessels; the deep inguinal nodes are their direct tributary, making this the pelvic continuation of the femoral lymphatic route.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Internal iliac (hypogastric) lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: pelvic viscera (rectum, bladder, uterus or prostate, vagina), deep perineal structures, and the gluteal region
notes: Follow the internal iliac vessels and their visceral branches; the principal nodal route for rectal, cervical and prostate cancer.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Obturator lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: bladder, prostate or cervix, and the obturator region
notes: Sit in the obturator fossa along the obturator vessels and nerve, at the junction of the external and internal iliac chains. Conventionally dissected with the external iliac group in pelvic lymphadenectomy, and often the first nodes sampled in prostate and cervical cancer staging.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Common iliac lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: the external and internal iliac node groups on that side
notes: Receive both the external and internal iliac chains before draining to the para-aortic nodes; a common site of nodal disease in cervical, prostate and bladder cancer staging.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: External iliac lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: deep inguinal nodes, bladder, proximal urethra, prostate or cervix, and lower anterior abdominal wall
notes: Lie along the external iliac vessels; the deep inguinal nodes are their direct tributary, making this the pelvic continuation of the femoral lymphatic route.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Internal iliac (hypogastric) lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: pelvic viscera (rectum, bladder, uterus or prostate, vagina), deep perineal structures, and the gluteal region
notes: Follow the internal iliac vessels and their visceral branches; the principal nodal route for rectal, cervical and prostate cancer.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Obturator lymph nodes
supplies_or_drains: bladder, prostate or cervix, and the obturator region
notes: Sit in the obturator fossa along the obturator vessels and nerve, at the junction of the external and internal iliac chains. Conventionally dissected with the external iliac group in pelvic lymphadenectomy, and often the first nodes sampled in prostate and cervical cancer staging.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
